top_story: On 23 November, Israel’s wartime imprint on Gaza sharpened from immediate violence into a deeper humanitarian and environmental emergency. Israeli strikes continued across the enclave, including in Jabalia, as the aid blockade and winter flooding compounded civilian exposure, while evidence that more than 99 percent of Gaza may now be contaminated by war-related pollutants pointed to a long-term public health crisis that will outlast active combat. Set against that destruction, Amazon’s $7.5 billion move to acquire an Israeli AI startup’s technology and absorb its staff underscored how Israel’s high-tech economy continues to attract major global capital even as Gaza’s civilian infrastructure collapses. The contrast highlights a widening regional reality in which economic normalization for Israel coexists with intensifying, durable harm to Palestinians.
